The '''2026–27 season''' is [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal Football Club]]'s 35th season in the [[Premier League]], their [[List of Arsenal F.C. seasons|101st consecutive season]] in the [[English football league system|top flight]] of English football, becoming the first team to spend over 100 consecutive seasons in the English top flight, and 110th season in the top flight overall. In addition to the [[2026–27 Premier League|domestic league]], Arsenal are also [[Participating management|participating]] in this season's editions of the [[2026–27 FA Cup|FA Cup]], [[2026–27 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]], [[2026 FA Community Shield|FA Community Shield]] and [[2026–27 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]], the latter of which is their [[Arsenal F.C. in European football|41st European campaign]]. The season covers the period from 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027.

==Review==
===Background===
Arsenal entered the season as the reigning league champions, having won the [[2025–26 Premier League]] title, their first top-flight title since the [[2003–04 Premier League|2003–04 season]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Arsenal end 22-year wait for Premier League title |url=https://www.premierleague.com/en/news/4662306/arsenal-win-2025-26-premier-league-title-ending-22-year-wait-to-be-crowned-champions-again |website=PremierLeague.com |publisher=Premier League |date=19 May 2026 |access-date=8 September 2026}}</ref> Arsenal made significant use of set pieces throughout the season, particularly from corners, scoring 25 set-piece goals (excluding penalties), the highest total in the league, while also setting a new record for goals scored from corners in a single Premier League campaign, with 19. Arsenal's defence was once again a key factor in their success. They kept a league-high 19 clean sheets, while conceding the fewest shots (310), shots on target (90), big chances (50) and expected goals (28.5) in the 2025–26 Premier League season. Their average of 0.7 goals conceded per game was also the lowest among clubs in Europe's top five leagues. The 19 clean sheets were Arsenal's most in a Premier League season since [[1998–99 Premier League|1998–99]], while [[David Raya]]'s 19 clean sheets matched the club record for a single Premier League season.<ref>{{cite web |title=27 great stats from our 2025/26 Premier League season |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/27-great-stats-from-our-2526-premier-league-season-ageBS3l8XFZn |website=Arsenal.com |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=8 September 2026}}</ref>

In Europe, Arsenal topped the [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League]] [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League#Table|league phase]] with a maximum 24 points from eight wins in eight matches, conceding only three goals. After defeating [[Sporting CP|Sporting]], [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]] and [[Atlético Madrid]] in the knockout stages, Arsenal faced [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] in the final, their first European final since the [[2019 UEFA Europa League final|2018–19 UEFA Europa League final]] and their first [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] final since the [[2006 UEFA Champions League final|2005–06 season]]. Arsenal lost the final 4–3 on penalties after the match ended 1–1 following extra time, despite completing their European campaign unbeaten.<ref>{{cite web |title=2025/26 UEFA Champions League |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/history/seasons/2026/ |website=UEFA.com |publisher=UEFA |access-date=8 September 2026}}</ref>

For the first time since the [[2016–17 Arsenal F.C. season|2016–17 season]], Arsenal are without [[Reiss Nelson]] after the club terminated his contract by mutual consent.<ref name="Nelson departs AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/reiss-nelson-leaves-arsenal-aK7qJ9T658rj |title=Reiss Nelson leaves Arsenal |date=2026-08-27 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=2026-08-27}}</ref> As a result of his departure, this is the first season that the squad does not contain a player that played under [[Arsène Wenger]], since before the debut of former captain [[Tony Adams]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mozzartsport.co.ke/football/news/after-43-years-last-link-to-wenger-is-gone-from-arsenal/68629 |title=After 43 years: Last link to Wenger is gone from Arsenal |date=2026-09-02 |website=Mozzart Sport |access-date=2026-09-03}}</ref>

===First team transfers (summer transfer window)===
The [[Premier League]]'s summer 2026 transfer window officially opened on 15 June and is scheduled to close on 1 September at 23:00 [[British Summer Time|BST]]. The window followed the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]], which was held from 11 June to 19 July 2026, meaning clubs could complete transfers both before and after the tournament.<ref>{{cite web |title=Summer Football Transfer Window 2026-27 Latest News |url=https://www.premierleague.com/en/transfers/2026-27/summer |website=PremierLeague.com |publisher=Premier League |access-date=24 August 2026}}</ref>

On 1 July 2026, Arsenal confirmed the permanent signing of defender [[Piero Hincapié]] from [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]], having activated the option to sign him permanently following his loan spell at the club.<ref name="Hincapié joined AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/piero-hincapie-joins-arsenal-in-permanent-deal-a64GQ9s3sBkl |title=Piero Hincapie joins Arsenal in permanent deal |date=2026-06-25 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=2026-09-10}}</ref> Hincapié made 39 appearances in all competitions during the 2025–26 season and helped Arsenal win the [[Premier League]] title.<ref name="Hincapié joined AFC"/> On the other hand, [[Karl Hein (footballer)|Karl Hein]] and [[Jakub Kiwior]] completed permanent transfers to [[SV Werder Bremen|Werder Bremen]] and [[FC Porto|Porto]], respectively, after their respective loan clubs exercised options to sign them permanently.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jakub Kiwior joins Porto on permanent deal |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/jakub-kiwior-joins-porto-on-permanent-deal-aIMXs2G4BAkI |website=Arsenal.com |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=24 August 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Karl Hein to join Werder Bremen on permanent deal |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/karl-hein-to-join-werder-bremen-on-permanent-deal-aFY2l5G8E22L |website=Arsenal.com |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=24 August 2026}}</ref>

On 9 July, free agent goalkeeper [[Illan Meslier]], formerly of [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]], signed a two-year deal with Arsenal, with the option to extend for a further year.<ref>{{cite web |title=Illan Meslier joins Arsenal |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/illan-meslier-joins-arsenal |website=Arsenal.com |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=24 August 2026}}</ref>

On 15 July 2026, [[Leandro Trossard]] left Arsenal to join Turkish [[Süper Lig]] side [[Beşiktaş J.K.|Beşiktaş]] for a reported £17.1 million. Trossard joined Arsenal from [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]] in January 2023 and made 174 appearances for the club, scoring 36 goals. During his time at Arsenal, he contributed to a number of important moments, including scoring the equalising goal against [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] in the [[2023 FA Community Shield|2023 Community Shield]] final and scoring a crucial late winner against [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] during Arsenal's [[2025–26 Premier League]] title-winning campaign. He helped Arsenal win the Premier League title in his final season at the club.<ref>{{cite web |title=Leandro Trossard joins Besiktas |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/leandro-trossard-joins-besiktas-a2RJl0E1RyLJ |website=Arsenal.com |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |date=15 July 2026 |access-date=24 August 2026}}</ref>

On 22 July 2026, Arsenal announced the signing of Greek forward [[Christos Tzolis]] from [[Club Brugge KV|Club Brugge]] on a long-term contract for £34 million. Tzolis joined Arsenal after an impressive 2025–26 season with Club Brugge, during which he helped the club win the [[2025–26 Belgian Pro League|Belgian Pro League]] title and was named the league's Player of the Season. He scored 22 goals and provided 29 assists in all competitions during the campaign.<ref>{{cite web |title=Christos Tzolis signs for Arsenal |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/christos-tzolis-signs-for-arsenal-axDM85b0dBUW |website=Arsenal.com |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |date=22 July 2026 |access-date=24 August 2026}}</ref>

On 5 August 2026, Arsenal confirmed the departure of [[Christian Nørgaard]] to [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] on a permanent deal.<ref>{{cite web |title=Christian Norgaard joins Everton |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/christian-norgaard-joins-everton-a7fZT9g6dECY |website=Arsenal.com |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |date=5 August 2026 |access-date=8 September 2026}}</ref>

On 8 August 2026, Arsenal signed Brazilian midfielder [[Bruno Guimarães]] from [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] for a reported £75 million.<ref>{{cite web |title=BBC Sport article |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c1719r079rjo |website=BBC Sport |access-date=8 September 2026}}</ref>

On 21 August 2026, Arsenal announced the signing of [[Ezri Konsa]] from [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] for a reported £55 million, with £51 million paid as a fixed fee and a further £4 million in potential add-ons.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ezri Konsa: Arsenal complete £55m deal for Aston Villa and England defender |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11677/13574990/ezri-konsa-arsenal-complete-lb51m-deal-for-aston-villa-and-england-defender |website=Sky Sports |date=21 August 2026 |access-date=8 September 2026}}</ref>

On 1 September 2026, [[Gabriel Jesus]] left the club to join [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]], while midfielder [[Fábio Vieira (footballer, born 2000)|Fábio Vieira]] joined [[Hamburger SV]] on a permanent deal following his loan spell.<ref>{{cite web |title=Gabriel Jesus joins FC Barcelona |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/gabriel-jesus-joins-fc-barcelona-aIweE9b0CIaV |website=Arsenal.com |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |date=1 September 2026 |access-date=8 September 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Fabio Vieira joins Hamburger SV in permanent deal |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/fabio-vieira-joins-hamburger-sv-in-permanent-deal-a8WYl8s7ALgc |website=Arsenal.com |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |date=1 September 2026 |access-date=8 September 2026}}</ref> Two days later, it was confirmed that [[Gabriel Martinelli]] joined Saudi Arabian club [[Al-Hilal SFC|Al-Hilal]] for £60 million, becoming Arsenal's record departure.<ref>{{cite web |title=Gabriel Martinelli joins Al-Hilal |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/gabriel-martinelli-joins-al-hilal-aOqHc1P93HkF |website=Arsenal.com |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |date=3 September 2026 |access-date=8 September 2026}}</ref>

On 16 August 2026, Arsenal began the season with a 3–0 victory over the [[2025–26 FA Cup|FA Cup]] winners [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] in the [[2026 FA Community Shield|Community Shield]] final, winning the competition for the 18th time in the club's history.<ref name="Arsenal 3-0 Manchester City">{{cite web |title=Arsenal 3-0 Manchester City |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/report-arsenal-3-0-manchester-city-axOZ78a0LKZm |website=Arsenal.com |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |date=16 August 2026 |access-date=24 August 2026}}</ref> Riccardo Calafiori opened the scoring in the 23rd second of the match, making it the fastest goal in Community Shield final history, after being played through on goal by [[Myles Lewis-Skelly]].<ref name="Arsenal 3-0 Manchester City"/> A header from [[Kai Havertz]] doubled Arsenal's lead, with new signing [[Christos Tzolis]] providing the assist following a curled cross from captain [[Martin Ødegaard]].<ref name="Arsenal 3-0 Manchester City"/> Tzolis provided another assist for Arsenal's third goal, finding Ødegaard inside the box, with the Norwegian sending [[Gianluigi Donnarumma]] the wrong way with a feint before calmly finishing into the empty net.<ref name="Arsenal 3-0 Manchester City"/> With his two assists, Tzolis became the first player to provide two or more assists in a [[FA Community Shield|Community Shield]] match since [[David Beckham]] did so for [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] against [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] in [[1996 FA Charity Shield|1996]].<ref name="Arsenal 3-0 Manchester City"/>

On 21 August, Arsenal began their title defence with a 3–0 home victory over newly promoted [[Coventry City F.C.|Coventry City]] in the [[2026–27 Premier League|Premier League]].<ref name="Arsenal 3-0 Coventry City">{{cite web |title=Arsenal 3-0 Coventry City |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/report-arsenal-3-0-coventry-city-an2Fq8x1O9cq |website=Arsenal.com |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |date=21 August 2026 |access-date=24 August 2026}}</ref> [[Kai Havertz]] opened the scoring with a composed finish following an assist from Riccardo Calafiori, before [[Bukayo Saka]] doubled the lead eight minutes later in the 23rd minute, calmly finishing in the empty net.<ref name="Arsenal 3-0 Coventry City"/> [[Martin Ødegaard]] added a third in the 49th minute, with his shot taking a deflection on its way into the net, securing Arsenal's first three points of the season.<ref name="Arsenal 3-0 Coventry City"/> New signing [[Christos Tzolis]] impressed once again, receiving praise from both supporters and the media.<ref>{{cite web |title=Christos Tzolis may have solved Arsenal's biggest weakness in bid to defend Premier League title |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/christos-tzolis-arsenal-coventry-b3037375.html |website=The Independent |date=22 August 2026 |access-date=24 August 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Summer signing Tzolis continues to impress |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cvgjg3g0v1no |website=BBC Sport |date=21 August 2026 |access-date=24 August 2026}}</ref> Ten days later, on 31 August, Arsenal secured a 1–0 away victory over [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] in the Premier League.<ref name="wg">{{Cite web |last=Coates |first=Live ReportingCharlotte |title=Aston Villa 0-1 Arsenal: Bukayo Saka scores winning goal for Gunners |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cr93ep2n2ppdt |access-date=2026-09-21 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> [[Bukayo Saka]] scored the only goal, sliding the ball into the net from a [[Riccardo Calafiori]] cut-back.<ref name="wg"/> [[Ezri Konsa]] also made his Arsenal debut as a substitute, becoming the first player since [[Petr Čech]] against [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] in 2015 to make his debut for a club against the team he had joined from.<ref name="wg"/>

=== September ===
On 6 September, Arsenal defeated [[Arsenal F.C.–Chelsea F.C. rivalry|London rivals]] [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] 2–1 at the Emirates Stadium in the Premier League. [[Morgan Rogers|Morgan Rodgers]] gave Chelsea the lead in the 2nd minute of the game, scoring the first goal Mikel Arteta's side has conceded this season. Kai Havertz equalised in the 25th minute, finding himself in a good position just outside of the box, before beating ex-Arsenal goalkeeper [[Emiliano Martínez|Emiliano Martinez]] at the near post. In the 50th minute, Christos Tzolis passed the ball forward, with Kai Havertz's clever dummy letting it go to captain Martin Ødegaard who slotted it in to give Arsenal the lead.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reporting |first=Live |title=Arsenal 2-1 Chesleas: Martin Odegaard sinks Chelsea in London derby thriller |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/ck1wx0010el5t |access-date=2026-09-21 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

On 9 September, Arsenal began their European campaign with a 1–0 win at [[Stadio Diego Armando Maradona|Diego Armando Maradona stadium]] against [[SSC Napoli|Napoli]]. Despite having 26 shots and 4.05 expected goals, Arsenal's only goal came from Martin Ødegaard's strike from the edge of the box, with Norwegian scoring his 4th goal in 5 matches.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Wright |first=Nick |date=10 September 2026 |title=Napoli 0-1 Arsenal |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/13582864/napoli-0-1-arsenal-martin-odegaard-goal-clinches-win-for-dominant-gunners-in-champions-league-opener |work=Sky Sports}}</ref> Three days later, Arsenal traveled to the [[Stadium of Light]] to face [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]]. After a goalless first half, Sunderland were given a controversial penalty after Ezri Konsa pulled [[Dan Ballard (footballer)|Daniel Ballard]] to the ground. Despite that, David Raya saved the penalty taken by [[Enzo Le Fée]] and two minutes later, [[Bruno Guimarães]] scored his first goal for Arsenal. Then in stoppage time, [[Reinildo Mandava]] fouled Bukayo Saka and was sent off after receiving a second yellow card. Saka converted the penalty that followed, and Arsenal won 2–0. <ref>{{Cite web |title=Sunderland 0-2 Arsenal: Bruno Guimaraes haunts Black Cats with stunner after David Raya penalty save |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/13583579/sunderland-0-2-arsenal-bruno-guimaraes-haunts-black-cats-with-stunner-after-david-raya-penalty-save}}</ref> Then in September 15th, Arsenal heavily rotated the squad for the EFL cup tie away at [[Portman Road]] to face Ipswich Town and prevailed 4–2 with a brace from Max Dowman and goals from Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino. <ref>{{Cite web |title=Ipswich vs Arsenal LIVE! Carabao Cup third round score updates, news, prediction, line-ups and how to watch or stream |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/live-blog/13586111/ipswich-vs-arsenal-live-carabao-cup-third-round-score-updates-news-prediction-line-ups-and-how-to-watch-or-stream}}</ref>Four days later, Arsenal faced Brighton away and lost 3–0 after goals from [[Pascal Groß]], [[Charalampos Kostoulas]], and [[Chema Andrés]]. This was the heaviest defeat for Arsenal since May 14, 2023 when they lost 3-0 at the Emirates, also to Brighton.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brighton 3-0 Arsenal: Mikel Arteta's side lose for first time this season as impressive hosts thrash defending champions |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/13586062/brighton-3-0-arsenal-mikel-artetas-side-lose-for-first-time-this-season-as-impressive-hosts-thrash-defending-champions}}</ref> With a Manchester City 5–3 win over Sunderland, City took first place with 15 points and Arsenal with 12 heading into the international break.

Over the international break, 17 players were called up for their national senior squad in September, Konsa,  Saka, Eze, and Lewis-Skelly ([[England national football team|England]]), Raya, Merino, and Zubimendi ([[Spain national football team|Spain]]), Timber ([[Netherlands national football team|Netherlands]]), Havertz ([[Germany national football team|Germany]]), Tzolis ([[Greece national football team|Greece]]), Odegaard ([[Norway national football team|Norway]]), Calafiori ([[Italy national football team|Italy]]), Gyokeres ([[Sweden men's national football team|Sweden]]), and Gabriel and Guimaraes (Brazil).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Peat |first=Charlie |title=17 stars called up for extended international break |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/17-stars-called-up-for-extended-international-break-a5ZYR8A13yx9 |access-date=2026-10-06 |website=Arsenal FC |language=en}}</ref>

=== October ===
On October 10, Arsenal defeated [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] at the Emirates, despite going a goal down following goals from Calafiori and Guimarães, both their first goals at home.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arsenal 2-1 Leeds: Riccardo Calafiori and Bruno Guimaraes on target as champions fight back to go level with Man City |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-leeds-united/report/559494 |access-date=2026-10-21 |website=Sky Sports |language=en}}</ref> Afterwards, on October 13 in the Champions League, [[Lille OSC]] traveled to the Emirates and were beaten 3–0 following goals from Timber, Eze, and Saka. <ref>{{Cite web |last=UEFA.com |title=Arsenal vs Lille: UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League phase |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2049572--arsenal-vs-lille/ |access-date=2026-10-21 |website=UEFA.com |language=en}}</ref> On October 18, 2026 Arsenal narrowly defeated Nottingham Forest following [[Noni Madueke|Noni Madueke's]] goal in the 80th minute to win 1–0.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nottingham Forest 0-1 Arsenal: Noni Madueke's late deflected strike wins it with Gunners' only shot on target |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/13598878/nottingham-forest-0-1-arsenal-noni-maduekes-late-deflected-strike-wins-it-with-gunners-only-shot-on-target |access-date=2026-10-21 |website=Sky Sports |language=en}}</ref>

===Kit information===
This is Adidas's eighth year supplying Arsenal kit, having taken over from [[Puma (brand)|Puma]] at the beginning of the [[2019–20 Arsenal F.C. season|2019–20]] season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/adidas-partnership-extended-to-2030-aGKOZ1n8fT3k |title=adidas partnership extended to 2030 |date=2022-09-30 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=2026-09-02}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.adidas.com/football/adidas-and-arsenal-launch-new-partnership-with-2019-20-home-kit/s/a792ee1b-7f39-4f66-a095-a689e151ec5b |title=adidas and Arsenal launch new partnership with 2019/20 home kit |date=2019-07-01 |website=Adidas |access-date=2026-09-02}}</ref>

*'''Home:''' The club revealed their new home kit for the 2026–27 season on 15 May 2026. The kit uses Arsenal's traditional colours of red and white. The shirt has a red body and white sleeves and is complemented by white shorts and red socks. Red shorts may be used in some away games when there will be a colour clash with the home team's kit. The shirt features subtle visual references to the [[Emirates Stadium]] to commemorate its 20 years as home of the club, including a bespoke collar inspired by the sweeping rooflines of the stadium.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/the-inspiration-and-features-behind-our-202627-home-kit-a84jJ7T0sFDo |title=The inspiration and features behind our 2026/27 home kit |date=15 May 2026 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=2026-09-02}}</ref> The kit was launched alongside a film named ''A Different Kind of Connection''.<ref>{{cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hGZSNVIhfBI |title=2026/27 Home Kit {{pipe}} A Different Kind of Connection |date=15 May 2026 |access-date=2026-09-02 |website=Arsenal F.C. |via=YouTube}}</ref>
*'''Away:''' On 24 July, the Gunners released their new away kit, which reimagines the club's Bruised Banana away shirt worn between [[1991–92 Arsenal F.C. season|1991]] and [[1992–93 Arsenal F.C. season|1993]]. The shirt features an engineered graphic inspired by the iconic geometric pattern, which, alongside the shorts and socks, are navy with coordinated red and yellow detailing. The shirt also features the adidas Trefoil logo, which was previously used on third kits.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/the-details-that-made-our-2627-away-kit-anvxx7n9cMEN |title=The details that made our 26/27 away kit |date=2026-07-24 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=2026-09-02}}</ref> Yellow shorts and socks may be used in away games in which there are a colour clash with the home team's kit. A week after the launch of the kit, the club released a feature-length video that detailed the full story behind the Bruised Banana pattern of the past and how it was modernised for the present day.<ref>{{cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3VJZIaDM_YI |title=ARSENAL BY DESIGN {{pipe}} The story of the Bruised Banana |date=2026-07-31 |access-date=2026-09-02 |website=Arsenal F.C. |via=YouTube}}</ref>
*'''Third:''' On 3 August, the club released their new third kit, which is inspired by the "belief, ambition and creativity" that defines the club. In addition to featuring the club's iconic lightning graphic, for the first time in five seasons, the shirt has the yellow base colour synonymous with Arsenal, as well as navy and burgundy details across the entire kit.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/a-state-of-mind-details-behind-our-third-kit-launch-astD91N3aisk |title=A state of mind: Details behind our third kit launch |date=2026-08-03 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=2026-09-02}}</ref> The shirt is complemented by navy shorts and socks, whereby yellow shorts and socks will be used in the away games in which there are a colour clash with the home team's kit. The kit was launched with an accompanying video named ''The Arsenal State of Mind''.<ref>{{cite AV media |title=THIRD KIT {{pipe}} The Arsenal State of Mind |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FYmtqplffbE |date=2026-08-03 |access-date=2026-09-02 |website=Arsenal F.C. |via=YouTube}}</ref>
*'''Goalkeeper:''' The new goalkeeper kits are based on Adidas's goalkeeper template for the season.
{{clear}}

==Pre-season and friendlies==
On 25 June, the club announced that their opening fixture of pre-season would be against [[Segunda División|Spanish]] side [[Girona FC|Girona]], who they had previously faced in the [[2024–25 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] in January 2025.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/mens-team-kick-pre-season-girona |title=Men's team to kick off pre-season in Girona |date=2026-06-25 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=2026-06-25}}</ref> Two months prior, the club confirmed that the squad would then travel to [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] for the first time since August 2018 to face another [[La Liga|Spanish]] side in [[Real Betis]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.arsenal.com/tickets/arsenal/2026-Aug-05/real-betis |title=Men's first team to play Real Betis in Dublin |date=2026-03-24 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=2026-07-05}}</ref> The club then confirmed their final two pre-season fixtures in quick succession, with [[Borussia Dortmund]] named as the season's [[Emirates Cup]] opponents,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/dortmund-confirmed-emirates-cup-2026-opponents |title=Dortmund confirmed as Emirates Cup 2026 opponents |date=2026-06-26 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=2026-06-26}}</ref> followed by a home fixture against [[Como 1907|Como]], who was managed by former Arsenal captain [[Cesc Fàbregas]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/arsenal-face-como-emirates-stadium-august |title=Arsenal to face Como at Emirates Stadium in August |date=2026-06-29 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=2026-06-29}}</ref>

===FA Community Shield===
{{main|2026 FA Community Shield}}
Arsenal, as [[2025–26 Premier League|reigning Premier League]] champions, played [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]], the winners of the [[2025–26 FA Cup]]. The fixture took place at the [[Millennium Stadium]] in [[Cardiff]] (which hosted the fixture between 2001 and 2006) instead of [[Wembley Stadium]] due to scheduling conflicts with a concert by [[the Weeknd]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://arsenal.com/news/2026-community-shield-take-place-cardiff |title=2026 Community Shield to take place in Cardiff |last1=Rogers |first1=Jonathon |date=2026-06-04 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=2026-06-04}} {{Dead link|date=October 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot}}</ref>

===EFL Cup===
{{main|2026–27 EFL Cup}}

The Gunners entered the EFL Cup in the third round as one of the Premier League teams participating in UEFA competitions. As a seeded team, they were drawn [[Portman Road|away]] to newly-promoted [[Premier League]] side [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/ipswich-town-drawn-in-carabao-cup-third-round-aXUPf9c4XH4Z |title=Ipswich Town drawn in Carabao Cup third round |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=2026-08-26 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=2026-09-18}}</ref> They were then drawn another [[Highbury Stadium (Fleetwood)|away]] tie to face [[EFL League Two|League Two]] side [[Fleetwood Town F.C.|Fleetwood Town]] for the first time in the club's history, in the fourth round.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/fleetwood-town-drawn-in-carabao-cup-fourth-round-aKHab3w54VHF |title=Fleetwood Town drawn in Carabao Cup fourth round |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=2026-09-16 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=2026-09-18}}</ref>

===UEFA Champions League===
{{main|2026–27 UEFA Champions League}}

As the champions of the [[2025–26 Premier League|Premier League]], Arsenal entered the UEFA Champions League in the league phase.

====League phase====
{{main|2026–27 UEFA Champions League league phase}}

Arsenal's [[UEFA coefficient#Men's club coefficient|UEFA club coefficient]] was 119.000 points at the end of the previous campaign.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/nationalassociations/uefarankings/club/?year=2026 |title=Club coefficients {{pipe}} UEFA rankings |date=2026-07-03 |website=UEFA |access-date=2026-08-27}}</ref> They were in Pot 1 for the league phase draw, which was held on 27 August 2026.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/02a8-21717d0c6cb5-03a9a5ff1552-1000--champions-league-league-phase-draw-pots-confirmed/ |title=Champions League: League phase draw pots confirmed |date=2026-08-27 |website=UEFA |access-date=2026-08-27}}</ref> Arsenal were randomly drawn to play [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] and [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] (for the second consecutive season) from Pot 1, [[Borussia Dortmund]] and [[Real Betis]] from Pot 2, [[Lille OSC|Lille]] and [[SSC Napoli|Napoli]] from Pot 3, and finally debutant [[Sabah FK (Azerbaijan)|Sabah]] and [[SK Slavia Prague|Slavia Prague]] from Pot 4.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/202627-champions-league-draw-our-eight-opponents-aatiP0f2okvk |title=2026/27 Champions League draw: Our eight opponents |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=2026-08-27 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=2026-08-27}}</ref>
